name: Crucible Industries Suppressed Compact SC-2 'Murmur'
description:
The SC-2 Murmur is an integrally suppressed submachine gun designed for industrial security operations where noise discipline is required — server farms, laboratory complexes, and medical facilities where gunfire causes equipment damage beyond the immediate engagement zone. The weapon's barrel is permanently enclosed in a suppression housing that reduces the 9mm subsonic report to levels below the threshold for triggering acoustic security alarms.

The Murmur uses a locked-breech design unusual for a 9mm SMG, eliminating the mechanical noise of a blowback bolt cycling. The result is a weapon where the loudest sound is the bullet's impact rather than its departure. Combined with subsonic ammunition, the SC-2 can be fired inside a server room without triggering decibel-sensitive fire suppression systems — a real operational concern in facilities where the equipment is worth more than the people.

Crucible markets the Murmur to facility security forces and specialized teams operating in noise-sensitive environments. At Φ4,200, it is priced for organizational procurement rather than individual purchase. The weapon is unremarkable in every way except its silence, which in the right environment is worth more than any other feature.
specifications:
caliber: 9mm subsonic caseless
effective_range: 50m
rate_of_fire: 600 rpm (cyclic)
magazine_capacity: 25 rounds
weight: 2.4 kg
tactical_use: The Murmur allows armed response in environments where the sound of gunfire causes more damage than the bullets. Server farms, clean rooms, laboratory complexes, and medical facilities all contain equipment that is sensitive to acoustic shock or decibel-triggered safety systems. The SC-2's below-alarm acoustic profile ensures that engaging a threat does not simultaneously destroy the facility's critical infrastructure.
cultural_context: The Murmur occupies a peculiar niche — a weapon designed to protect things that are damaged by weapons. Its existence reflects the priority hierarchy of corporate facilities: equipment first, then data, then personnel. Security forces carrying Murmurs are sometimes called 'librarians' — they enforce silence as a professional requirement.
story_hooks: A data center heist went undetected because the thieves used stolen Murmurs — the acoustic security system never triggered, and the camera footage showed muzzle flashes with no corresponding audio alerts.
A Murmur was used in an assassination at a medical facility. The suppressed weapon was so quiet that patients in adjacent rooms heard nothing — the body wasn't discovered for hours.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, business-like submachine gun with an unusually bulbous forward section. The integral suppression housing dominates the weapon's silhouette, giving it a swollen, almost organic appearance compared to conventional SMGs. Despite its lethal purpose, it reads as industrial and clinical rather than aggressive — the aesthetic of a precision tool rather than a combat arm.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 34cm | Barrel length: 10cm (enclosed within suppression housing) | Width: 5cm | Height: 12cm (including charging handle)
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and compact at 2.4kg — feels substantial without being cumbersome. The weight is distributed forward due to the suppression housing, creating a natural point-of-aim feel. Designed for one-handed control in confined spaces.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer frame with steel internals. The suppression housing is titanium-aluminum composite (excellent acoustic absorption properties). Stainless steel internal components.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal gray polymer with brushed stainless steel accents on the bolt carrier. The suppression housing has a subtle anodized finish that dampens reflection — deliberate anti-glint treatment. Wear reveals darker bare metal underneath.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: Matte charcoal gray polymer | Accent: Brushed stainless steel | Secondary: Anodized titanium (suppression housing) in neutral gunmetal
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured synthetic rubber grip with subtle radial scoring for wet-glove purchase. Minimalist, ergonomic, designed for industrial safety wear. No aggressive texturing — this is a facility security weapon, not a combat platform.
distinctive_features: Integrated suppression housing with seven baffle stages visible through inspection ports
Locked-breech delayed action system (unusual for 9mm — visible in bolt carrier design)
Subsonic ammunition counter on left side of frame (mechanical dial, Φ cost-saving measure)
Heat dissipation fins on suppression housing (matte-black anodized, functional and intentional)
Charging handle positioned high and rear for operation with mounted optics
Integrated picatinny rail system along top for mounting facility-standard sights
Magazine well with witness holes (round count visibility)
No muzzle brake or flash hider — the entire muzzle is enclosed
Wear patterns consistent with server room environments (cable abrasion marks on the grip, dust accumulation in suppression housing vents)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible Industries logo (stylized 'C' in a circle) stamped on the left side of the polymer receiver above the trigger guard. 'SC-2 MURMUR' engraved in small block letters on the suppression housing. Serial number plate on the right side of the frame, laser-etched. Manufacturer origin stamp: 'VERDURE GARDEN SUPPLY - ASSEMBLED GLMZ' in tiny print above the magazine well.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained with field wear. Polymer shows scuffing consistent with secure storage and industrial transport. Suppression housing vents contain residue from subsonic powder (lighter, less sooty than standard ammunition). Charging handle shows polish from frequent operation. No rust — stainless components, but visible fingerprints and dust from server farm environments. This is a working tool, not a showpiece.
